answer: Epoch-overlap action fingerprinting is a cross-epoch consistency rule. It compares each identity’s conditional action rates on shared recurring contexts across adjacent epochs using Jensen-Shannon divergence. If divergence exceeds 0.15 or probe coverage is below 80%, rewards are withheld until three epochs match. One probe routes a timber batch. Another labels a knoll image. A third checks terrain on a mesa. Each clone must run probes, store histories, and keep policies synchronized; per identity this costs continuous compute/storage and at least one epoch’s rewards.
